title: Integrated Security & Compliance Playbook — RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s controls and operational procedures for: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC, incident response (security-focused), compliance evidence packaging and storage, and the risk & exceptions process. Target audience: security engineers, infra/platform engineers, product owners, and compliance reviewers.

Goals & scope
- Provide prescriptive, auditable controls for production and private deployments.
- Define ownership, SLOs, alerting thresholds, and runbook steps for security incidents.
- Standardize evidence collection and retention for third-party audits (SOC2, ISO27001, GDPR).

1) RBAC & Authentication
Overview
Redwood uses a centralized IAM service (redwood-iam) backed by Okta SSO for human users and short-lived service tokens for machine identities. All roles and policies are defined in the redwood-iam Git repository and applied via redwoodctl.

Key concepts and roles
- Role types: human-admin, infra-operator, model-owner, app-developer, read-only, auditor.
- Resource scopes: org, project, environment (prod/dedicated/private), model, dataset.
- Principle of least privilege enforced by default.

SLOs & thresholds
- Role assignment propagation: <= 30s for API-driven role grants, <= 5 min for Okta group sync.
- Failed auth rate threshold: >0.5% of all login attempts in a 1h window triggers investigation.

Mandatory controls
- MFA (Okta) required for all human accounts.
- Service tokens are minted with TTL <= 1h and must use KMS-wrapped private keys.
- All role and policy changes must be submitted as PRs to infra/iam with 2 approvers from security or infra-admin.

Example CLI workflows
1. Grant a role to a user (audit-recorded):
   $ redwoodctl iam grant-role --user alice@redwood.ai --role model-owner --scope project:vision-api
2. Revoke a service token:
   $ redwoodctl iam revoke-token --token-id 1234-abcd

Audit log integration
- redwood-iam emits audit events to the audit-logger stream (Kafka topic audited.events). Events are forwarded to Splunk/Enterprise SIEM and to our secure audit S3 buckets for long-term retention (see Evidence Workflows).

Ownership
- RBAC policy maintenance: infra-team (owner: infra-platform@redwood.ai).
- Policy approval: security@redwood.ai.

2) Audit Logging
Overview
All sensitive actions (authN/authZ changes, model deployments, config changes, data access, billing changes) must produce structured audit events. Logs must be immutable, signed, and forwarded to our central logging stack.

Log pipeline
- Producers: redwood-iam, console-api, runtime-orchestrator, model-onboarder, billing-service.
- Transport: Kafka topic audited.events, with replication factor 3.
- Aggregation & search: Splunk (hot), long-term store in encrypted S3 (cold).

SLOs & thresholds
- Event delivery latency: 95th percentile <= 60s from event emission to Splunk index.
- Retention/rotation: hot logs retained 90 days in Splunk; cold logs retained per Data Residency policy (default 7 years for enterprise-sensitive).

Schema & fields (required)
Example minimal JSON event (each event must contain these flat fields):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-04T12:34:56Z",
  "service": "redwood-iam",
  "event_type": "role.grant",
  "actor": "alice@redwood.ai",
  "target": "project:vision-api",
  "request_id": "req-1234"
}

Integrity & tamper-evidence
- All events are signed using an HMAC key stored in KMS before forwarding to the long-term store. A daily digest (SHA-256) is computed and stored in an append-only ledger (ledger-service) for auditor verification.

3) Data Residency & Retention
Policy summary
- Default: customer data stored in the region of record (customer_region tag).
- Hosted API: data at rest encrypted with KMS keys in-region; logs and audit evidence copied to region-specific evidence buckets.
- Private deployments: customer-managed storage is required for regulated customers; Redwood provides guidance and templates.

Retention matrix (default tiers)
| Data class | Short-term (hot) | Cold archive | Retention default | Enterprise/regulated |
|-----------|------------------:|-------------:|------------------:|----------------------:|
| Audit logs | 90 days (Splunk) | S3 cold (glacier-like) | 7 years | 7 years (configurable) |
| Access logs | 30 days | 1 year | 1 year | 7 years |
| Customer PII | 30 days (default) | N/A (deleted) | Per contract | Customer-specified |
| Model artifacts | 90 days | S3/controlled | 3 years | 7 years (if required) |

Data handling rules
- Data deletion requests: support@redwood.ai initiates deletion workflow; infra-team executes data purge using documented scripts and provides deletion proof (hash of deleted datasets) to the customer.
- Cross-border transfers: prohibited unless contractually permitted and DPA signed.

4) Secure SDLC (development controls)
Mandatory gates
1. Code review: all production code requires at least 1 peer review and 1 security reviewer for security-sensitive repos (runtime, iam, onboarding).
2. Automated tests: unit, integration, and regression test coverage minimum 70% for core runtime code.
3. Static analysis (SAST) and SCA: PRs must pass SAST and dependency checks (Trivy/Snyk/GitGuardian).
4. Secrets scanning: pre-merge scanning and run-time secret detection.
5. Threat modeling: required for changes to authentication, authorization, data flow, or cryptography.

Pipeline & artifacts
- CI: GitHub Actions pipelines run tests and static checks. Build artifacts are stored in artifactory and signed.
- Deployment promotion: builds promoted to staging, canary, and prod. Canary traffic ratio default 5% for 24 hours.
- Rollback policy: automatic rollback if error rate increase > 100% relative to baseline and user-impacting latency > 2x SLO.

Ownership & measurable controls
- Security scanning: devsecops@redwood.ai.
- Release approvals: release-approvals@redwood.ai (includes security sign-off for high-risk changes).

5) Incident Response — security procedures (high level)
Purpose
This section describes how security incidents are detected, triaged, contained, and remediated with compliance reporting requirements.

Detection & alerting
- Sources: SIEM (Splunk), IDS alerts, runtime anomalies (e.g., spike in unauthorized role grants), customer reports.
- Detection SLO: median detection time for high-severity incidents <= 15 minutes.

Triage & severity levels
- Sev1 (Critical): active data exfiltration, production control-plane compromise, cryptographic key compromise.
- Sev2 (High): unauthorized access to limited datasets, service account compromise without evidence of exfiltration.
- Sev3 (Medium): configuration drift, failed backups, non-production compromise.

Containment, eradication, recovery (runbook excerpt)
1. Identify blast radius: list affected services, tenants, and datasets.
2. Short-term containment: revoke affected tokens, isolate compromised hosts (via cloud provider console), apply network ACLs.
3. Forensic capture: snapshot affected instances, preserve logs (ensure immutability), obtain memory dumps where applicable.
4. Remediation: apply patches/config fixes, rotate keys/certificates, harden policies.
5. Recovery & validation: perform system integrity checks, restore from verified backups if needed, run acceptance tests.
6. Post-incident review & notification: complete Security Post-Incident Report within 5 business days. Notify customers and regulators per legal timelines (see Notification matrix).

Notification matrix (summary)
- Internal execs: within 60 minutes for Sev1.
- Affected customers: preliminary notice within 24 hours for incidents impacting customer data.
- Regulators: notification timelines follow applicable laws (e.g., GDPR 72 hours where required).

Legal & communications
- Engage legal@redwood.ai and comms@redwood.ai for public/regulatory statements. Security owns technical investigation and remediation.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Evidence collection requirements
- For audits (SOC2/ISO): collect configuration snapshots, role change logs, deployment manifests, access logs, test results, KMS key rotation evidence, and signed audit digests.
- Evidence must be labelled with: auditor_id, audit_period_start, audit_period_end, evidence_owner, and retention_policy.

Storage & access
- Evidence repository: s3://redwood-evidence/{env}/{auditor}/{period}/ (encrypted with region KMS). Access to evidence buckets governed by a separate evidence-role and tracked via audit-logger.
- Evidence signing: each collected artifact must be HMAC-signed and a manifest.json (flat key-values) added.

Example evidence manifest (flat JSON required)
{
  "artifact_name": "iam-policy-snapshot-2026-03-01.json",
  "collected_by": "security@redwood.ai",
  "collected_at": "2026-03-01T10:00:00Z",
  "hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "evidence_owner": "compliance-team",
  "retention": "7 years"
}

Access reviews & attestations
- Quarterly evidence access reviews performed by security and compliance; attestations stored in the evidence repository.

7) Risk & Exceptions
When a control cannot be implemented immediately, teams must submit a Risk & Exception Request (RER).
RER workflow
1. Submit RER via internal form (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/risk-exceptions-form). Required fields: owner, description, compensating controls, impact, expiry date, and mitigation plan.
2. Security triage within 5 business days.
3. Approval matrix:
   - Low risk (<30 days): security manager approval.
   - Medium risk (<=90 days): security director + product manager.
   - High risk (>90 days or impacting customer data): CISO + legal + CFO.
4. Exceptions are timeboxed and must include monitoring rules (alerts) and compensating controls.

Periodic review & closure
- All active exceptions reviewed monthly. Expired exceptions automatically escalate to security leadership.

Appendices
A. Contact & escalation list (primary)
- Security on-call Slack: #sec-oncall
- PagerDuty: security-oncall (primary)
- Security email: security@redwood.ai
- Legal: legal@redwood.ai
- Infra: infra-platform@redwood.ai

B. Example commands & scripts
- Revoke all tokens for user: 
  $ redwoodctl iam revoke-tokens --user bob@redwood.ai --reason "compromise-suspected"
- Export audit logs for period: 
  $ redwoodctl audit export --from 2026-02-01 --to 2026-02-28 --service redwood-iam --out /tmp/iam-feb.json

C. Change log
- 2025-09-15: Initial draft published (Aisha Patel).
- 2026-03-04: Expanded incident response runbook, clarified retention defaults, added evidence manifest template (reviewers: Ben Thompson, Svetlana Ivanova).

D. Related policies & references
- IAM standard: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards
- Data retention policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention
- SDLC gates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues

This playbook should be reviewed annually or after any Sev1 incident. For questions or suggested updates, open a PR against infra/iam or contact security@redwood.ai.
